claims.text: The claim that BOTH goods and services consumer spending rose in May 2021 is contradicted by the BEA release: services spending increased while goods spending decreased.

counterarguments.text: One could note that current-dollar total consumer spending did increase in May, and that the PCE price index from a year earlier rose for both goods and services — but that is a price comparison over 12 months, not a monthly spending change, so it does not support the claim.

citations.quotation: Thepersonalconsumptionexpenditures(PCE)price indexforMay increased3.9 percentfromoneyearago, reflectingincreasesin both goodsand services.

limitations: The excerpt does not provide the May 2021 dollar changes in goods spending or services spending separately, so the magnitude of the offset between the goods decrease and services increase cannot be quantified from the supplied text.
The provided excerpts are partial coverage of the BEA release; detailed tables with goods vs. services monthly changes are not included.
The release is dated June 25, 2021 for the period May 2021; publication and reference period dates are as declared in the text.
